relevance_note: The paper reports one adult patient with an individual-level description who carries a TNFAIP3 variant: "a variant of uncertain significance (c.63A>T (p. I21 = ) variant in the TNFAIP3 gene)", plus his tested relatives.
method_note: Case report, no tables; nothing was transcribed by script. I read the whole Markdown file (including the Figure 1 legend) and verified every span character by character with literal searches, so unusual characters (U+2010 hyphen, U+2009 thin space) are reproduced exactly. In scope: the patient (no label of his own, so 'patient'), his father and sister (carry the same variant) and his mother (tested, no variant). Variant string recorded as the cDNA part with the protein part in its own field; the paper prints the variant four times in slightly different ways (c.63A>T, c.63 A>T, P.I21=, p. I21 = ). D-29: for the father and sister I left pathogenicity, variant type, functional evidence and ACMG 'not reported' because the paper states these for the patient's variant, not for theirs; zygosity and the variant string come from the Figure 1 legend sentence that names the father and the sister explicitly. Inheritance for the patient is 'inherited paternal' because the father carries the same variant; the mother was tested and does not. No variant row was created for the mother, because no variant is tied to her ('no variant in the TNFAIP3 gene was found in the sample of the patient's mother'). For the father and sister the paper says only that they "appeared without any discomfort yet carrying mutant genes"; I did not turn this into phenotypic_features rows or checklist 'excluded' values because it is a general statement of no discomfort rather than a named abnormality, so their checklist items stay 'not reported'. The patient's VUS is treated as a variant the paper describes for him (it is not dismissed as non-causal). The patient's symptom onset is given only as 'an intermittent fever for more than 1 year' at age 25 years; no age at diagnosis is stated (genetic testing is dated 2022, without an age).
